name: Battle of Stalingrad
kicker: WWII’s Eastern Front turning point · Soviets encircled a trapped German army
briefing: In the summer of 1942, German forces pushed deep into southern Russia, aiming to seize oil fields in the Caucasus and capture a city on the Volga River that bore the Soviet leader’s name. Street-by-street fighting dragged on for months around landmarks like Pavlov’s House and the hill of Mamayev Kurgan, until a massive Soviet counterattack, Operation Uranus, encircled the German Sixth Army. Its surrender in February 1943 marked the turning point of World War II’s Eastern Front.

qb.tip: Operation Uranus and the trapped German Sixth Army under Friedrich Paulus are in almost every tossup; Pavlov’s House and Mamayev Kurgan are the next-most-common stock clues.

sample.note: 9 real QBReader tossups for this answer line (4 Middle School/Easy High School + 5 Regular High School, power-marked)

tossups.p: An anti-aircraft regiment staffed largely by young women helped defend this battle’s namesake city. Fighting here earned the grim nickname “Rat War” from German soldiers because of brutal house-to-house combat. A famous photograph from the ruins shows a fountain statue of children dancing in a circle, still standing amid the wreckage.
tossups.r: Operation Uranus, launched in November 1942, encircled the trapped German Sixth Army here. For 10 points, name this World War II battle fought in a city on the Volga River.

tossups.p: Soviet sniper Vasily Zaytsev [“ZYT-sef”] became famous for his skill during this battle. It grew out of Germany’s Case Blue offensive, which aimed to seize oil fields in the Caucasus. A small Soviet garrison held out for about two months inside a ruined apartment block called Pavlov’s House.
tossups.r: German commander Friedrich Paulus was promoted to field marshal just before becoming the first German field marshal ever to surrender. For 10 points, name this battle, the turning point of the Eastern Front.

tossups.p: Fighting in this battle reached the floor of a tractor factory that had been turning out T-34 tanks. Control of the hilltop Mamayev Kurgan [“mah-MY-yev koor-GAHN”] changed hands repeatedly, and a giant statue called The Motherland Calls stands there today. Soviet generals Georgy Zhukov and Aleksandr Vasilevsky [“vah-see-LEV-skee”] planned the encirclement that trapped the German attackers.
tossups.r: It began under the shadow of Stalin’s Order No. 227, which threatened to punish any soldier who retreated. For 10 points, name this World War II battle fought in southern Russia.

tossups.p: This battle’s defenders included an anti-aircraft regiment staffed largely by young women. It turned back the German invasion that began with 1941’s Operation Barbarossa. German soldiers grimly nicknamed the brutal house-to-house combat here the “Rat War.”
tossups.r: It took place where the Don and Volga Rivers run close together in southern Russia. For 10 points, name this battle often called history’s deadliest, fought from 1942 to 1943.

tossups.p: This battle included a two-month stand by a small Soviet garrison inside a ruined apartment block called Pavlov’s House. It grew out of Germany’s Case Blue offensive, which had aimed at Caucasus oil fields. Operation Uranus, launched in November 1942, encircled the German Sixth Army trapped inside the city.
tossups.r: It ended in February 1943 with the surrender of that encircled army. For 10 points, name this battle fought in a city named for the Soviet leader.

tossups.p: Soviet planners won this battle partly by targeting weaker Romanian units guarding the German flanks. A famous photograph from its ruins shows a fountain statue of children dancing in a circle. German commander Friedrich Paulus was promoted to field marshal just before surrendering.
tossups.r: Control of the hilltop Mamayev Kurgan changed hands many times during this battle. For 10 points, name this turning point of World War II’s Eastern Front.

tossups.p: This battle lasted roughly five months, from the summer of 1942 into the following winter. It was planned in its final stage by Soviet generals Georgy Zhukov and Aleksandr Vasilevsky. Soviet sniper Vasily Zaytsev became a celebrity for his skill here.
tossups.r: It turned back the invasion begun by Germany’s Operation Barbarossa and became the Eastern Front’s turning point. For 10 points, name this battle fought over a city on the Volga River.

tossups.p: This battle began under the shadow of Stalin’s Order No. 227, which threatened to punish retreating soldiers. German soldiers grimly nicknamed its brutal house-to-house fighting the “Rat War.” A tractor factory that had been producing T-34 tanks became an unlikely battlefield.
tossups.r: Operation Uranus encircled the German Sixth Army here in November 1942. For 10 points, name this battle, often called history’s deadliest, fought in a city on the Volga River.

tossups.p: This battle’s Soviet defenders included a small garrison that held Pavlov’s House for about two months and an anti-aircraft regiment staffed largely by young women. It grew out of Germany’s oil-driven Case Blue offensive into the Caucasus. Control of Mamayev Kurgan changed hands repeatedly.
tossups.r: It ended with the surrender of the trapped German Sixth Army in February 1943. For 10 points, name this turning-point battle of the Eastern Front.

tossups.p: This battle made a celebrity of Soviet sniper Vasily Zaytsev. Soviet planners targeted weaker Romanian units on the German flanks to make their encirclement work. A famous photo of a fountain statue of dancing children survived amid its ruins.
tossups.r: Roughly two million total casualties make it history’s deadliest single battle, by some counts. For 10 points, name this World War II battle named for the Soviet leader’s city.

tossups.p: This battle’s fighting reached a tractor factory that had been turning out T-34 tanks. Operation Uranus, launched in November 1942, trapped the German Sixth Army inside the city. German commander Friedrich Paulus was promoted to field marshal just before his surrender.
tossups.r: It lasted roughly five months, from the summer of 1942 into the next winter. For 10 points, name this battle on the Volga River that turned the tide of World War II.

tossups.p: This battle featured a two-month Soviet stand at Pavlov’s House and a long struggle for the hilltop Mamayev Kurgan, now home to the statue The Motherland Calls. Generals Zhukov and Vasilevsky designed the encirclement that decided it. It turned back the invasion begun by Operation Barbarossa.
tossups.r: It was fought in a city on the Volga River named for the Soviet leader. For 10 points, name this turning point of the Eastern Front.

tossups.p: This battle grew out of Germany’s Case Blue push for Caucasus oil fields. Soviet forces exploited weaker Romanian units guarding the flanks to close their encirclement. German soldiers bitterly nicknamed its building-to-building combat the “Rat War.”
tossups.r: It ended in February 1943 when the trapped German Sixth Army finally surrendered. For 10 points, name this costly battle of World War II’s Eastern Front.

tossups.p: This battle is remembered for Pavlov’s House, a ruined apartment block held by a tiny garrison for two months, and for the repeated fighting atop Mamayev Kurgan. Vasily Zaytsev’s sniping made him famous during it. Stalin’s Order No. 227 had forbidden retreat without permission as it began.
tossups.r: Operation Uranus encircled the German Sixth Army here in November 1942. For 10 points, name this battle, often considered history’s deadliest.

tossups.p: This battle’s defenders included a mostly female anti-aircraft regiment and a garrison holding out in Pavlov’s House. It grew from the Case Blue offensive toward Caucasus oil and turned back the invasion begun by Operation Barbarossa. Soviet generals Zhukov and Vasilevsky closed the encirclement that trapped the German Sixth Army.
tossups.r: It was fought where the Don and Volga Rivers run close together. For 10 points, name this turning-point World War II battle named for the Soviet dictator’s city.

trap.title: The Battle, or the Man?
trap.body: Because the city of Stalingrad was named for Joseph Stalin, this battle shares many clues with him: the Sixth Army, Order No. 227, and the Eastern Front. It is also easy to mix up with Operation Barbarossa (the 1941 invasion that opened the Eastern Front) and the Battle of Kursk (a later tank battle on the same front).
trap.fix: “Name this battle” or “this siege” wants Stalingrad; “name this leader” wants Stalin himself. Barbarossa was the 1941 invasion; Kursk came half a year later and featured the largest tank battle in history, not Pavlov’s House or Operation Uranus.
trap.line: Real answer line: Battle of Stalingrad (accept Siege of Stalingrad)
